Rounds
for recuperative care

The shift on one screen.
You tap. You sign.

Built with and for the LVNs and medical assistants at Illumination Health + Home. Med pass, med rec, handoff and notes, without typing into forms, and nothing that says something you didn't.

Who needs you now

Beds colored like a restaurant floor: teal breathes for an open med pass, coral for a miss, green for caught up. Tap a bed to work it.

Ordered vs. taken

Drop Kipu's two exports in. Rounds matches them and shows missed doses, refused doses, and meds with no order, before a payer does.

Nothing you didn't say

Notes are drafted from your own jottings. Touch any line and the jotting it came from lights up. Anything added gets caught in red.

"If they took it and you didn't document it, the insurance company isn't going to pay."IHH staff, describing why every med pass log matters. Rounds makes the log the tap itself.
1
Start your shiftSay your name. See the floor. The handoff from the last shift waits at the top until you've read it.
2
Work the bedsMed pass taps, vitals tiles, "they said," "I taught." Or say it: the mic understands "blood pressure 120 over 80 for Robert" and asks before it logs.
3
Sign and sendYour note in your words, copied into Kipu. A teach sheet for the client in English or Spanish. A handoff for the next shift.
  • Everything stays on the device. Rounds never writes to Kipu, CalOptima or any IHH system.
  • Names and ID numbers are removed in the browser before any text is sent for drafting.
  • Every drafted line is checked against your words by a deterministic checker, not by trusting the model.
  • Open source (MIT), built at the Orange County Claude Impact Lab, October 17, 2026, donated to IHH.
